newsitem.title: CHINA: China says foreign reserves ensure economic safety.
newsitem.headline: China says foreign reserves ensure economic safety.

text.p: China's huge foreign exchange reserves, which hit $120.94 billion at end-June, are needed to guarantee economic and political stability, the People's Daily said on Thursday.
"Foreign exchange reserves are not only economic reserves but are also strategic reserves," the newspaper said.
"Discussion of the appropriate size of the foreign exchange reserves must begin with national economic safety and political stability," it said.
The large reserves, second only to Japan's, were needed to help offset financial risks in China's balance of payments and to stabilise exchange rates for the local yuan currency, it said.
The reserves would also help to pay back China's foreign debt, which topped $116 billion at the end of 1996, it said.
Beijing aimed to repay about $20 billion of debt and interest each year, it said but gave no further details.
The funds could also be used for credit to help ailing state enterprises, it said without elaborating.
